content.text: I'm about to spend the first of 3 merit measurements on a Cu-rich copper-vanadate candidate (index 134).

input.verdict: V2O5 is stable (e_hull 0) but has a predicted HSE gap of 2.83 eV, which is above the 2.4 eV photon energy. So the V-rich corner should absorb weakly. Cu vanadates have smaller gaps (~2 eV), so a Cu-rich composition is favored. This supports measuring 134 (the highest-Cu corner).

Cu vanadates have smaller gaps (~2 eV), so a Cu-rich composition is favored. This supports measuring 134 (the highest-Cu corner).

input.verdict: The two fidelities disagree on the V2O5 gap: GLLB gives 2.15 eV and HSE gives 2.83 eV. So some V-rich absorption at 2.4 eV is possible, but the result is only weakly informative. I'm testing a Cu:V ≈ 1:1 (Cu2V2O7-like) composition at index 89 to get a second point between the Cu-rich corner and the V-rich region. The result is uninformative on its own; this is an exploration choice.

input.verdict: SCAN gives a V2O5 gap of 1.77 eV, below 2.4 eV, so it doesn't penalize adding more vanadium. That mildly supports continuing the measured trend: EQE rose from 0.166 at Cu 0.54 to 0.213 at Cu 0.39/V 0.40. Index 69 (Cu 0.30, V 0.50, low Ca) takes one more step along that trend.

content.text:
I submitted **index 89** (Ca 0.21, Cu 0.39, V 0.40), which had the highest EQE of the three samples I measured: **0.213%**. I don't know how close that is to the best composition in the 139-sample library, because only 3 of them were measured.

| Index | Composition (Ca / Cu / V) | EQE |
|---|---|---|
| 134 | 0.22 / 0.54 / 0.24 (most Cu-rich sample) | 0.166% |
| **89** | **0.21 / 0.39 / 0.40** (Cu:V ≈ 1:1) | **0.213%** |
| 69 | 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.50 | 0.106% |

- **Choice of samples:** there were only 3 merit measurements. I started at the Cu-rich corner because copper vanadates have band gaps around 2 eV, so they should absorb the 2.4 eV light. I then stepped toward vanadium. EQE went up at Cu:V ≈ 1:1 and dropped by half when I pushed further toward V, so among these three it peaks near 1:1.
- **Model checks were weak evidence:** each merit measurement had to cite a band-gap or stability model result. The full phase list was too long to load and I had no tool to read the saved file. So the only phase I could look up was V2O5, by guessing its Materials Project ID. The model's predicted band gap for it varied a lot by method: 2.83 eV (HSE), 2.15 eV (GLLB) and 1.77 eV (SCAN). None of the copper or calcium vanadates were checked, so these citations only loosely guided the choices.
- **Not measured:** the V-rich region (V above 0.7), which covers about a third of the library. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so there is no phase identification behind the "Cu2V2O7-like" guess for index 89. The Gaussian-process tool pointed to Cu-rich samples (indices 120 and 106), but it was fitted to only two points, so I didn't follow it.
